case_name: Gogireddy Sambireddy vs Gogireddy Jayamma And Anr.

parties.respondent_defendant: Gogireddy Jayamma And Anr. (wife and another)

facts_of_case: A Hindu wife laid a complaint against her husband for marrying a second wife, seeking an offence under Section 494, I.P.C., read with Sections 11 and 17 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: Discrimination forbidden by Article 15(1) is based solely on the ground of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth, and not on other grounds.
legal_principles.held: What the article forbids is discrimination and discrimination based solely on all or any of the grounds mentioned in the Article. All differentiation is not discrimination, but only such differentiation as is invidious and as is made because of some characteristic or affiliation which is either disliked or not regarded with equal favour but which has no rational connection with the differentiation made as a justifying reason.
cited_cases: Anjali Roy v. State of West Bengal, (Year)
Gogireddy Sambireddy vs Gogireddy Jayamma And Anr., (Year)

legal_principles.principle: The discrimination forbidden by Article 15(1) must be based solely on the ground that a person belongs to a particular race or caste or professes a particular religion or was born at a particular place or is of a particular sex.
legal_principles.held: A discrimination based on one or more of these grounds and also on other grounds is not hit by the Article.
cited_cases: Anjali Roy v. State of West Bengal, (Year)
Gogireddy Sambireddy vs Gogireddy Jayamma And Anr., (Year)

legal_principles.principle: The Legislature must have discriminated only on one of those grounds and no other factor could possibly have been present.
legal_principles.held: If the Legislature has discriminated only on one of those grounds and no other factor could possibly have been present, then undoubtedly the law would offend against Article 15(1).

legal_principles.principle: The Legislature must not have considered other factors in making the law.
legal_principles.held: If religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth is merely one of the factors which the Legislature has taken into consideration, then it would not be discrimination only on ground of that fact, but if the Legislature has discriminated only on one of those grounds and no other factor could possibly have been present, then undoubtedly the law would offend against Article 15(1).

use_for_drafting: representing clients in Hindu marriage disputes
